solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One mostly aiming for a threesome in bed?

definitions.text: One mostly aiming for a threesome in bed?

blocks.clueFragment: One mostly aiming for a threesome in bed?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone with a racy ambition for the bedroom
setter's reading: a bed is a scoring segment of a dartboard, and the treble bed is what a competitor at the oche chiefly aims to land three in

explanation.walkthrough: The bedroom picture is pure misdirection: on a dartboard the narrow scoring rings are called beds, and the treble 20 bed is the usual target.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor at the oche spends most throws trying to hit the treble ring, the board's most valuable target.

clue.text: First of dudes DEA hope to bust?

definitions.text: First of dudes DEA hope to bust?

indicators.note: first of tells us to keep only the opening letter of the word that follows
to bust is to break apart, so the letters are smashed up and rebuilt

blocks.note: opening letter of dudes
taken as written

explanation.surface: American drug agents hope to arrest the leading dude of some gang.
explanation.walkthrough: The DEA is the US Drug Enforcement Administration; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since a drug user is exactly whom they would hope to bust.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual drug user is just the sort of person narcotics agents would aim to arrest, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: Function held by Supremes singer is ruddy quality

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside its grip, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Diana Ross, lead singer of the Supremes
the sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A Motown star's role is described as having a ruddy character.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosiness is the state of being rosy, a pink or reddish glow, which is what ruddy describes.

clue.text: One Direction's Harry taking line gets complaints

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, so a letter is removed from the name

blocks.note: Harry Styles was a member of the boy band One Direction
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A pop star doing a line of something earns complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking line' suggests drug use, but taking means removing the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Styes are small painful eyelid infections, the kind of minor ailment a doctor would call a complaint.

clue.text: Endure life primarily with drop of alcoholic beer

indicators.note: primarily points to the very first letter of the word before it
a drop is a tiny amount, here just one opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: opening letter of life
opening letter of alcoholic
stout is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Survive life chiefly by sipping strong beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endure' looks like an instruction to the reader, but it is the definition: to last out is to survive to the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To last out means to survive or persist until the end of some ordeal, a phrasal synonym for endure.

clue.text: With bit of yeast, bread maker takes longer

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter

blocks.note: opening letter of yeast
bread is slang for money, so a bread maker is someone who makes money

explanation.surface: A baker adding a little yeast needs more time for the loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longer' reads as more time, but it is a noun: one who longs. Bread is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A longer is one who longs for something, and a yearner is someone who yearns, the same craving.

clue.text: Religious type can initially grimace expelling gas

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
a tin is a can
opening letter of grimace

explanation.surface: A cleric's face twists as he breaks wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbiting is British slang for talking on and on (from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk); gas is idle chatter, so expelling gas is just that.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to chatter idly, and rabbiting means talking at tedious length, so both describe pouring out empty talk.

clue.text: After having bottom pinched, beat jerk

indicators.note: having the bottom pinched means the last letter has been stolen away

blocks.note: a tick is a single beat of a clock

explanation.surface: Someone has their bottom pinched and hits the creep who did it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes jerk an insult; it is the definition in its sense of a sudden twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary twitch of a muscle, a sudden jerk.

clue.text: Tenor associated with composer and Journey

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor
Maurice Ravel was a French composer; associated with just joins him on

explanation.surface: A singer linked to a composer and to the rock band Journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital J makes Journey look like the band; it is the plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel is to make a journey from one place to another; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: I follow with clubs if villain switches lead to clubs

indicators.note: switching the lead means the first letter is swapped for something new

blocks.note: a baddie is a villain
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs; this is the second clubs in the clue

explanation.surface: A henchman trails behind a weapon-carrying villain who changes to cudgels.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person: the answer itself says I follow (a golfer) carrying clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie walks the golf course behind a player, carrying the bag of clubs.

clue.text: Unhealthy-looking food parcel from Cornwall?

blocks.note: first meaning: pale and sickly in complexion
second meaning: a pastry case folded around meat and vegetables, the Cornish speciality

explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county in south-west England famous for its savoury pastry turnovers; the question mark marks the playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for a pale sickly face and the noun for a Cornish meat-and-vegetable pastry.

clue.text: Directors after top player to create the right side

blocks.note: a star is a leading performer
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Executives hired after a star signing put the club on the right path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the directors second.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the nautical term for the right-hand side of a ship as one faces forward.

clue.text: Will nurses start to suture with complete ease?

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the first word cradles the next letter inside it
the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to will property is to hand it down to an heir
opening letter of suture

explanation.surface: Can hospital staff begin stitching a wound without any difficulty?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a future auxiliary and 'nurses' like hospital staff; they are the verb bequeath and the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To win hands down is to win effortlessly, so the idiom means with no trouble at all.

clue.text: Old folk at home gyrating on methamphetamine

indicators.note: gyrating means spinning round, so the phrase before it is turned back to front

blocks.note: ice is street slang for crystal methamphetamine
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Elderly people dance around the house high on crystal meth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old folk' suggests pensioners; it means an ancient people. 'On' places the turned piece after the drug in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe, led by Boudicca, so they are a people of long ago.

clue.text: A seaman needing to be picked up in storm

indicators.note: picking something up can mean hearing it, so we go by how the words are spoken

blocks.note: a salt is an old sailor, and a salt said aloud matches the answer

explanation.surface: A sailor in a gale needs rescuing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' sits naturally beside a seaman as weather, but it is a verb: to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to attack it violently, which is what an assault is.

clue.text: What a Wonderbra is doing is raising spirits

blocks.note: first meaning: a push-up bra lifts the bust
second meaning: cheering someone up

explanation.walkthrough: The Wonderbra is a famous push-up bra brand; the joke is that it raises things in the literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the action of lifting something upwards and an adjective for anything morale-boosting.

clue.text: With head of Battersea off, mind cats and dogs?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
off means taken away, so that letter is removed from the following word

blocks.note: opening letter of Battersea
the brain is the seat of the mind

explanation.surface: Battersea is a London district with a famous home for stray dogs and cats, so the clue nods to its animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea Dogs and Cats Home is a well-known London animal shelter, which makes cats and dogs read as pets; it is the idiom for heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is raining cats and dogs is an idiom for a downpour, so the phrase stands in for heavy rain.

clue.text: Ideas go all over the shop on necking new port

indicators.note: all over the shop means in a chaotic mess, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
necking means swallowing, so the jumbled letters take another inside them

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A drinker's ideas scatter after necking a fresh glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: Necking is British slang for drinking quickly, and port looks like the drink; it is the harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a major Californian harbour city and naval base, so it is a port.

clue.text: Very large pork pies and fast-food burgers

blocks.note: first meaning: huge lies; pork pies is rhyming slang for lies
second meaning: the big burger sold by Burger King

explanation.walkthrough: Pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, which is why the surface sounds like a food list. The burger is Burger King's signature sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means outrageous falsehoods and is also the brand name of a large fast-food hamburger.

clue.text: In the sack, foremost of lushes spilled claret

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another
the foremost part of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the sack is slang for bed
opening letter of lushes

explanation.surface: A drunk in bed knocks over a glass of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is a Bordeaux red wine, which fits the drunks, but it is also slang for blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is slang for blood, so spilling claret means losing blood, which is what bled says.

clue.text: Soprano visiting dry place will have peach Melba?

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: a desert is an arid region
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A singer performing in the arid outback is offered a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Peach Melba was created for the Australian soprano Nellie Melba, which is why a soprano appears; the question mark shows it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Peach Melba, peaches with raspberry sauce and ice cream, is an example of a sweet course eaten after the main meal.

clue.text: Who has pants stuffed with German baloney?

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the words before it are poor as they stand and get rearranged
stuffed with means filled with, so one letter goes inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Someone asks who has underwear filled with German sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is British slang for rubbish as well as underwear; baloney reads as the sausage but means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash and baloney are both informal words for nonsense or foolish talk.

clue.text: Chief expression that a call centre worker wears?

definitions.text: Chief expression that a call centre worker wears?

blocks.clueFragment: Chief expression that a call centre worker wears?
blocks.note: surface reading: the main facial look an operator puts on for the job
setter's reading: chief can be the head, and a set is a fixed look

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wears' suggests a facial expression, as in wearing a smile; in fact the worker wears equipment over the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Call centre staff wear a combined earphone and microphone over their head to take calls.

clue.text: Disregard V-sign or earthily-gesticulated displays

indicators.note: displays means shows openly, so the answer is on view inside the words before it

blocks.note: runs across V-sIGN OR Earthily
surface padding completing the picture of rude gestures

explanation.surface: Ignore rude gestures made crudely in public.
explanation.walkthrough: A V-sign is the British rude hand gesture of two raised fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay it no attention, which is what disregard means.

clue.text: Agent about to take on extravagant snooker player?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word before it is read the other way
to take on is to absorb, so the turned word holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: a rep, or representative, acts as an agent
OTT, over the top, means extravagant

explanation.surface: A sports agent is about to sign a flamboyant snooker player.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: anyone who sinks balls in snooker does this.
explanation.definitionFit: To pot a ball is to sink it into a pocket, so a snooker player can be called one who pots.

clue.text: Turn and fall asleep

blocks.note: first meaning: become sour or spoiled, as milk does
second meaning: drift into sleep

explanation.walkthrough: Turn looks like rolling over in bed; here it means food spoiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to spoil, as milk turns sour, and to drop off to sleep.

clue.text: Following manhandling, rusted tap began to move

indicators.note: manhandling means roughly forcing about, so the letters are pushed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: After some rough handling, a seized tap finally turned.
explanation.definitionFit: When an engine or machine started up it began running, so the phrase means it set in motion.

clue.text: Locum employed originally in ancient Greek valley

indicators.note: originally points to how a word begins, its very first letter

blocks.note: a locum is a stand-in worker, a temp
opening letter of employed

explanation.surface: A stand-in worker once had a job in classical Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: A locum is a temporary stand-in, usually a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe is a gorge in Thessaly celebrated by classical poets as a beautiful valley.

clue.text: It's so rude to relocate immigrants

indicators.note: to relocate is to move things to new positions, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that relocating newcomers is impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relocate' sits naturally with immigrants in the surface, which hides that it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcomers from abroad are people from outside a community, so outsiders is a looser synonym.

clue.text: Fancy that looker? I seriously doubt it!

blocks.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise, like fancy that!
an eye is what one looks with

explanation.surface: Someone eyes an attractive person, then scoffs at the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy that looker' reads as desiring a good-looking person; it splits into an exclamation and an organ of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: My eye! is an old-fashioned exclamation of disbelief, rejecting what has just been said.

clue.text: Be in terror of missing out on female attention

indicators.note: missing out on something means going without it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to fear is to be in terror
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Someone dreads being ignored by women.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone's ear, or give an ear, is to have their attention, so the word stands for listening notice.

clue.text: Visit the races or decline in a shocking manner?

blocks.note: first meaning: attend greyhound racing
second meaning: deteriorate badly

explanation.walkthrough: The dogs is British slang for a greyhound racing meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a trip to greyhound racing, the idiom also means to fall into ruin or a terrible state.
